transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I guess it’s the eating. It’s gotten kind of out of hand. Most nights, after my wife goes to bed, I end up in the kitchen and I’ll eat way past what would be a normal plate. Like, if there’s fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls—especially if we had people over or there are leftovers from some event, you know how everybody sends food home and then it’s just sitting there—I’ll just keep going.

I don’t mean just grabbing a snack. It’ll be like a whole tray is gone, or it feels like half the fridge, and then I’m standing there wondering what I just did. That’s mainly why I’m here.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop yourself or control how much you're eating during these episodes?

Yeah… yeah, that’s probably the part that scares me the most. It’s like once I take that first bite, the decision’s already been made somewhere without me. I’ll be standing there saying in my head, “George, stop now, you don’t need another plate,” and then my hands are still fixing one anyway, or I’m opening up another container.

It’s weird because I can tell myself not to do it—I mean, I’ll even pause sometimes—but then I’m right back in it. Like when my aunt used to send home those big foil pans after church things, everybody acts like leftovers are a blessing, and I guess they are, but for me it’s like… I don’t know, once it starts, I can’t seem to put the brakes on.
Do you usually feel guilty or ashamed after these eating episodes?

Yeah… guilty, ashamed, all of that. Afterward I feel sick with myself. Like, during the day people see me as this organized guy, you know, the one who’s supposed to have it together, be strong, handle things. And then there I am at night, sitting with wrappers or empty containers around me, just disgusted that I let it happen again.

It’s hard to even look at myself sometimes after. I’ll think, “How did you do this again?” and then I just feel… embarrassed, even if nobody saw it.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating during these episodes?

Not really, no. I mean… I can be telling myself the whole time, “George, stop, that’s enough,” and it’s like my body didn’t get the message. Once I take that first bite, it feels like the decision’s already been made for me.

I’ll start fixing another plate or opening another container, even while I’m thinking I shouldn’t. It’s not like when you just choose to have seconds at a cookout or something—my uncle used to always say, “Go on, don’t waste food,” and everybody would laugh—but this doesn’t feel like that. It feels like I’m watching myself keep going and I can’t quite grab hold of it.
Do you feel like you're eating really quickly during these episodes?

Yeah… I do. I eat fast, really fast. Like, embarrassingly fast sometimes.

I used to actually enjoy cooking, you know—seasoning things right, taking my time with it. My mother used to say you could tell when somebody cared about a meal by how they stood over the pot. But during those episodes, I’m not even tasting it like that. I’m just getting it down.

Sometimes I’ll be standing right there at the counter, not even sitting like a normal person, swallowing these big bites before I’ve even finished chewing the last one. It’s like I’m rushing, but I don’t even know what I’m rushing for.
Do you usually eat like this when you're feeling stressed, anxious, or upset?

I don’t know if I can say that for sure. I mean… sometimes I’m already wound up, yeah, but I haven’t really tracked it like that.

Stress is funny, because I used to think stress was just when you had a deadline or somebody yelling at you, you know? My dad used to get quiet when he was stressed, just sit with the TV on and not really watch it. I think about that sometimes. But with me, I don’t always know what I’m feeling before it happens. Sometimes I only realize something was off afterward.

So… I guess I’m not sure. It might be connected, but I couldn’t point to it cleanly and say, “That’s why.”
Do you think your eating episodes are triggered by feeling upset or emotional?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I know people say emotional eating, and maybe that’s part of it, but I don’t always have a clear feeling right before it happens.

Sometimes I’ll look back and think, well, maybe I was upset about something, but in the moment it’s not like I’m saying, “I’m sad, so I’m going to eat.” It’s more muddy than that. My sister used to be very clear about her feelings—she’d tell you exactly what she was mad about, every detail—and I’m kind of the opposite. I can go half the day not realizing something bothered me.

So… I can’t honestly say yes or no. I haven’t noticed a clean pattern like that.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over time because of these eating episodes?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I don’t weigh myself regularly, and honestly I avoid the scale a lot.

My clothes fit different sometimes, but then I’ll tell myself maybe they shrank, or it’s the dryer, or I’m just bloated that day. My aunt used to say dryers ruin everything, which—maybe that’s not really the point.

So… significant changes? I don’t know. I can’t say clearly. I haven’t really kept track of it in a way where I could tell you.
Do you feel guilty or ashamed because you couldn't stop eating or control how much you ate during these episodes?

Yeah… yes. That part I do know.

Afterward I feel… I don’t know, sick with myself. Like I’m supposed to be this put-together guy—people see me as organized, dependable, strong, whatever—and then I’m sitting there looking at what happened and I feel ashamed. Guilty. Disgusted with myself, honestly.

It’s strange because I can handle other things. I used to be the person people asked to organize stuff, make a plan, keep things moving. Even in school, group projects, I’d end up being the one with the folder and the schedule. So when I can’t seem to stop myself with this, it hits me hard. Like, how did I let it happen again?

So… yeah. There’s definitely shame afterward. More than I like admitting.
How often do these eating episodes happen?

For months now, I don’t think there’s been a single week where it hasn’t happened at least once.

Most weeks it’s… more than that. Several nights, usually after my wife goes to bed. That sounds so planned when I say it, and I don’t mean it like I’m marking it on a calendar or anything. It’s just that the house gets quiet, and then it’s easier to sort of… I don’t know, slip into it.

But yeah, if you’re asking how often, it’s not rare. It’s been every week, and a lot of weeks, several times.
Do you feel any sense of relief after these eating episodes are over?

I’m not sure I’d call it relief. Maybe for a second there’s just… quiet? Like the urge isn’t yelling at me anymore.

But “relief” sounds too clean, I guess. It’s not like finishing a big project or when you finally pay a bill you’ve been avoiding. I remember once I had this whole stack of overdue mail and when I finally sorted it, that was relief. This is… different.

Afterward I mostly just sit there and feel kind of blank, and then I start thinking about what just happened. So if there is relief, it’s not something I really notice clearly.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating during these episodes, or is it more like something is controlling you?

It feels more like something else is running it, honestly.

I mean, I know that sounds dramatic. It’s not like I black out or anything. I’m there. I know what I’m doing. But once I take that first bite, it’s like… the decision already got made somewhere without me. And I’ll actually be thinking, George, stop now. Just stop. Put it away.

And then my hands are still fixing another plate, or I’m opening another container like I didn’t just tell myself not to. It reminds me—well, not reminds me exactly, but I used to be good at stopping things before they got out of hand, like with projects or budgets or whatever. I could see the steps. With this, I can see it happening, but I can’t seem to interrupt it.

So no, I don’t feel in control in those moments. Not really.
Have these eating episodes caused you any physical health problems?

I don’t know, not in any clear way that I can point to.

I mean, I feel awful after, but I’m not sure if you mean like… actual medical problems. I haven’t really sat down and made a list or anything. I tend to avoid thinking about that stuff, honestly. My dad was the same way with doctors—he’d say, “If you don’t look, it can’t be bad,” which is obviously not good advice, but I guess I picked up some of that.

So… I can’t say for sure. I haven’t noticed something specific that I’d call a physical health problem from it.
Have you gained a significant amount of weight since these eating episodes started?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I mean, my clothes fit differently sometimes, but then I also have clothes from like ten years ago that probably shouldn’t be the measuring stick for anything.

I don’t weigh myself much. I kind of avoid it. I had an old scale in the bathroom for years, and at some point the battery died, and I just… never replaced it. Which is maybe an answer in itself, I guess, but I can’t give you a number or say it’s been significant.

So, I don’t know. I haven’t really been tracking it.
Do you think your eating episodes are usually preceded by feeling anxious, stressed, or upset?

I don’t know if I’ve really noticed a pattern like that.

I mean, sometimes I’m stressed, sure, but that’s just kind of life, isn’t it? Bills, family stuff, the whole thing. And then other times it happens when nothing big is going on, or at least nothing I can put my finger on. I’ll think back afterward and try to figure out what set it off, and then I get distracted thinking about whether I missed something earlier in the day, like an argument or an email I didn’t answer, and then it turns into this whole detective thing.

So… maybe sometimes, but I can’t honestly say they’re usually preceded by anxiety or being upset. I haven’t tracked it closely enough to know.
Do you feel like you're unable to control how much you eat during these episodes because you feel an intense urge to continue eating?

Yeah… yes, that part I can say pretty clearly.

It’s like once I take the first bite, something kind of switches over. Not in a dramatic way, I guess, but it feels like the decision’s already been made for me. And I’ll be thinking, George, stop now, just put it away, you don’t need more, but at the same time I’m already getting up or fixing another plate or opening another container.

It’s strange because I’m aware of it while it’s happening. Like I’m not confused about what I’m doing. I just… don’t feel like I can stop it in that moment.
Do you consider these episodes of eating to be binge eating?

I mean… I guess so, yeah. I don’t know exactly where the line is, like what officially counts, but what brings me in is that most nights, after my wife goes to bed, I end up in the kitchen and it turns into way more than just a snack.

Like, I’ll start with leftovers or whatever’s there, and then it’s a plate of fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls… and then I’m still going. If there are event leftovers or something in the fridge, I can get through a whole tray, or it feels like half the fridge is gone before I really stop.

So, yeah, if that’s what you mean by it, then I’d probably call it that.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the eating episodes qualify as binge eating, which most directly relates to eating an unusually large amount of food during discrete episodes.

patient.answer:
I mean… I guess so, yeah. I don’t know exactly where the line is, like what officially counts, but what brings me in is that most nights, after my wife goes to bed, I end up in the kitchen and it turns into way more than just a snack.

Like, I’ll start with leftovers or whatever’s there, and then it’s a plate of fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls… and then I’m still going. If there are event leftovers or something in the fridge, I can get through a whole tray, or it feels like half the fridge is gone before I really stop.

So, yeah, if that’s what you mean by it, then I’d probably call it that.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms align with the diagnostic criteria for Other Eating Disorders, specifically binge eating disorder, characterized by recurrent episodes of eating a large quantity of food in a short period, feeling a lack of control during these episodes, and experiencing guilt and shame afterward.
